carmen: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about transport resume heuristics for air-gapped bundle transfers and an operator playbook. Wanted to capture tradeoffs before we finalize the agent API.

mohit: +1. We need to decide whether resume is file-chunk-oriented (idempotent by chunk hash) or stream-offset oriented (byte offset + signature). Both have pros/cons for memory and verification.

jules: chunk hashes make verification simpler offline: you can verify each chunk as it lands. But reassembly ordering and partial manifests gets tricky for very large bundles.

sara: stream-offset is simpler for resuming after flaky transfers — resume at offset N and continue — but you lose the ability to prove partial integrity without re-scanning. Also harder with compressed or encrypted streams unless we use fixed-size encrypted blocks.

mohit: Ops constraints: on-prem customers have limited disk and intermittent carriers. Chunked approach lets us apply chunks as they arrive and free the carrier sooner. But chunk manifests grow and we need a pruning strategy.

carmen: Proposal: hybrid model — use fixed-size content-addressed chunks (e.g., 4MB) + a lightweight chunk index manifest that is itself signed. Transfer can resume at chunk boundaries. Each chunk has a hash; agent verifies per-chunk on write.

ops-bot: deploy-bot uploaded bundle:rd-2026-03-15-cc53 to S3-proxy (meta: size=18GiB, chunks=4600).

jules: Hybrid sounds good. Follow-up: how do we handle partial-apply visibility to operators? If an admin aborts mid-apply, we need clear operator-level signals and deterministic rollback or cleanup.

carmen: Operator playbook (draft): 1) start transfer -> agent logs received-chunks count. 2) When chunk count >= 100% but pre-apply hooks not run, agent writes activation marker to /var/lib/redwood/activation.pending. 3) admin runs `redwood apply --dry-run` to inspect. 4) admin triggers `redwood apply --commit` which atomically renames activation.pending -> activation.active. If apply fails, agent leaves activation.failed with reason and chunk-level hashes for retry.

mohit: That naming dance is good. We should also include a tombstone timestamp and operator-visible rewrite key so on reconnect we can detect stale partials. E.g., activation.pending.{bundle-id}.{attempt-id}.{ts}.

sara: What about memory and verification costs? Verifying 4MB chunks is cheap, but scanning 4600 chunk hashes on every restart is non-trivial. Suggest an on-disk Bloom filter or a lightweight compact bitmap of received chunks to avoid re-hashing everything.

jules: Bitmap + periodic checkpoint makes sense. Also need to account for signer's public key rotation: manifest signature verification must record signing-key-id so agent can fetch previously trusted keys from local keyring before verifying older bundles.

carmen: Agree. Operationally: when a transfer resumes, agent should: (a) consult chunk-bitmap, (b) request only missing chunk ranges, (c) verify per-chunk hash on write, (d) update bitmap and persisted progress marker. No global re-hash.

mohit: Edge case: what if a chunk is corrupted in transit but hash matches due to attacker collision? We rely on manifest-level signature to prevent tampering — so make manifest sign the sorted list of chunk hashes and include bundle-level metadata (size, seq). That makes collision attacks infeasible.

sara: Add KMS/HSM note: in private deployments where manifest signing keys are customer-managed, the agent must accept an allowlist of key-IDs. If the key is remote (HSM), agent should cache verified key fingerprints to avoid network calls during apply.

jules: Rollback semantics: if apply fails mid-activation, we should support two modes: "clean-up" (delete partials and restart) and "resume" (keep partials and resume at chunk boundary). Default should be resume to reduce bandwidth. Clean-up requires operator confirmation.

carmen: UX proposal for console: show progress as chunk ranges (e.g., 0-1200/4600), last successful chunk hash, activation state, and recommended action buttons: Resume / Cleanup / Inspect. Also show replay-safety note: resume only at chunk boundary; compressed streams not supported for partial-resume unless chunked before compression.

mohit: Testing plan: create flaky network harness with reorders, corruptions, and restart scenarios. Verify bitmap sync and no double-apply. Add e2e test where manifest key rotates mid-transfer and agent picks up older key from keyring.

sara: One more tradeoff: chunk size. 4MB target seems good for most networks; smaller chunks increase metadata but improve resume granularity. We should expose a per-customer chunk-size knob at packaging time.

carmen: Next steps: I'll update the RFC with the hybrid-chunk index format (proto sketch), activation marker naming, bitmap format, and operator playbook. Action items: @mohit to draft the manifest proto (include key-id and chunk hash list), @jules to draft console UX mockups, @sara to design the bitmap on-disk layout. We'll sync tomorrow. :+1:
